name: Activate
definition: Getting a new user to take their first meaningful action in a product, beyond signing up.
sampleObjectives: Increase the share of new sign-ups who complete a first core action within 24 hours

patternLinks.rationale: Starting visibly at the lowest named tier, with a concrete next step shown, gives a new user an immediate, low-effort action to take.

name: Repeat
definition: Increasing how often a user performs a core action over time, from occasional to frequent use.
sampleObjectives: Increase weekly active usage among users who have already activated
Grow the share of users completing the core action at least five days a week

patternLinks.rationale: A visible, resettable count of consecutive days directly targets repetition of a specific qualifying action.
Lowering the bar required to count as 'done that day' is a direct lever on repetition frequency, as seen in Duolingo's own change.
A short, time-boxed comparison with others gives a recurring reason to act within the window.
A timely prompt close to a deadline is a direct intervention aimed at getting one more repetition in before the window closes.
A persistent, visible record of daily activity can make recent gaps salient, nudging a user to act again today.
An ongoing, repeatable benchmark gives a standing reason to return and improve a ranked result.
An accumulating balance that grows with each qualifying action gives a standing reason to keep acting rather than stopping once a single reward is claimed.
A challenge spanning several days requires repeated qualifying actions within the window, not a single one-off action.

name: Sustain
definition: Maintaining an existing level of participation over a longer period, resisting the natural tendency for engagement to decay.
sampleObjectives: Reduce month-over-month decline in active streak/usage counts
Increase the share of engaged users still active after 90 days

patternLinks.rationale: The mechanic's entire purpose is maintaining an unbroken run, directly targeting sustained participation.
Mutual stakes with another person are intended to make a lapse feel costlier, supporting sustained participation.
A recurring daily goal with visible closure gives a reason to keep returning rather than letting the habit lapse.
Reminders near a deadline are a direct lever against the natural decay of participation.
A long-running visible history gives a reason not to let a well-established record lapse, even without a formal streak rule.
A shared, ongoing collective target gives participants a reason to keep contributing rather than stopping after one session, since the group total is still accumulating.

name: Complete
definition: Finishing a defined task or journey end-to-end, rather than stopping partway through.
sampleObjectives: Increase the completion rate of a multi-step task or course
Reduce drop-off at known abandonment points in a journey

patternLinks.rationale: An explicit visual signal of closure (the ring joining up) marks the moment of completion itself.
Awards granted on reaching a milestone give a tangible marker that a task or stage was actually finished.
The challenge explicitly marks completion as a distinct, defined end-state rather than letting the activity trail off indefinitely.
Reaching the top named tier is itself the explicit completion state the pattern is built around.

name: Explore
definition: Prompting a user to try something unfamiliar within a product, rather than repeating only what they already know.
sampleObjectives: Increase the share of users who try a feature or content category outside their usual pattern
Grow discovery of underused parts of a product's catalogue

patternLinks.rationale: Surfacing a user's own listening/activity back to them can highlight items or patterns they hadn't consciously noticed, a mild prompt toward exploring their own data — though this is a secondary effect, not the pattern's main purpose.

name: Deepen
definition: Increasing the skill, effort or commitment a user brings to an activity they already do.
sampleObjectives: Increase average session depth or difficulty level chosen by returning users
Grow the share of users opting into a more demanding tier of an activity

patternLinks.rationale: The goal-intensity setting is a direct lever on how much effort a user commits per session.
Milestone awards tied to personal bests can encourage pushing effort further than the minimum required.
Tracking and visibly marking a user's own best result directly targets improving skill or effort on a familiar task.

name: Connect
definition: Getting users to interact with, collaborate with, share with, or compete against other users.
sampleObjectives: Increase the share of users with at least one active social connection in-product
Grow the volume of user-initiated shares of in-product content

patternLinks.rationale: The mechanic only functions between two or more connected users, directly targeting interaction.
Comparing scores against others is a direct, if lightweight, form of competitive connection.
The pattern's shareable format is explicitly designed to be posted and seen by others, turning private data into a social object.
A shared, ranked comparison against other participants is a direct form of competitive connection.
Making a user's activity visible on a public profile is a direct, if passive, way of connecting with other users.
Aggregating participants' activity into one shared goal is itself a direct form of connection, even without any individual comparison or ranking.

name: Contribute
definition: Getting users to create value for others, rather than only for themselves.
sampleObjectives: Increase the volume of user-generated content or help offered to other users
Grow participation in peer-support or peer-accountability features

patternLinks.rationale: Sending a nudge to a friend whose streak is at risk is a small act of contributing to someone else's consistency, not just your own.
A public record of contribution activity is itself a form of visible contribution to a shared project or community.
Making contribution activity visible to others is a direct way the pattern surfaces value created for a wider community, not just the user themselves.

name: Switch
definition: Getting a user to adopt an alternative behaviour in place of an existing one.
sampleObjectives: Increase adoption of a new default or recommended option over the previous one
Reduce reliance on a behaviour the product is trying to move users away from
